sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Dvaita Philosophy**: Postulates that the world is real and not an illusion (Maya), and there is an eternal, fundamental difference between God (Vishnu) and the individual soul.
• **Tattvavada**: The school of thought founded by Madhvacharya, meaning 'the doctrine of reality'.
• **Five-fold Differences (Pancha-bheda)**: The core of Dvaita—difference between God and soul, God and matter, soul and soul, soul and matter, and matter and matter.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Unlike Shankara’s 'Nirguna' (attributeless) Brahman, Madhva advocated for 'Saguna' (with attributes) Brahman, identifying Vishnu as the supreme reality.

items.definition: Eight monasteries established by Madhvacharya in Udupi to propagate Dvaita philosophy and manage the Krishna temple.
A rotational system of worship and administration among the eight mathas, ensuring institutional continuity.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Bhakti as Liberation**: Emphasized that devotion is the only path to salvation, accessible to all regardless of caste.
• **Institutionalization**: Established a robust monastic order (Mathas) that preserved Vedic traditions in South India.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Intense theological debates with Advaitins and Vishishtadvaitins.
• **Solutions**: Prolific writing of commentaries (Bhashyas) on the Prasthanatrayi (Upanishads, Bhagavad Gita, Brahma Sutras).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'MAD-V-A' (Madhva = Dvaita = A-bheda/Bheda).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Madhva taught that the soul and God are 'Bheda' (different), unlike Shankara who taught 'Abheda' (non-different).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Madhvacharya with Ramanujacharya. Remember: Ramanuja = Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Monism); Madhva = Dvaita (Dualism).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Tattvavada' to demonstrate depth of knowledge regarding the ontological realism of the Dvaita school.

keyTakeaways: Madhvacharya founded the Dvaita school, asserting the eternal reality of the world and the distinction between God and soul.
He established the Ashta Mathas in Udupi, creating a sustainable institutional model for Bhakti propagation.
His philosophy serves as a critical counter-narrative to the Advaita (monist) school of Adi Shankara.
